desc:
A histogram has bars of width 1 and heights heights[i]. A rectangle inside it covers bars l..r (consecutive, l ≤ r) and has a positive integer height not above the shortest of those bars.

Call a rectangle maximal if it cannot be made bigger inside the histogram: it cannot be made taller, and it cannot be extended by one bar to the left or to the right. Two maximal rectangles are different when their bar ranges l..r differ. Return the number of maximal rectangles.

Example: for [2, 1, 2] the maximal rectangles are bars 0..0 (height 2), bars 2..2 (height 2) and bars 0..2 (height 1), so the answer is 3. For [2, 3, 2] the answer is 2: bar 1 alone (height 3) and bars 0..2 (height 2).
hints: A maximal rectangle is determined by its bar range: its height must equal the minimum of that range, and the bars just outside the range must be strictly shorter than that minimum (or not exist). A bar of height 0 can never be part of one.
For each bar, the range where it is a minimum is bounded by the nearest strictly shorter bars. Several bars of equal height can describe the same range; count each range once.

Scan left to right with a stack of strictly increasing positive heights. Popping a height (because a strictly shorter bar arrived) closes exactly one maximal rectangle; a bar equal to the top is not pushed again.
editorial: Keep a stack of strictly increasing positive heights, one entry per rectangle that is still open. For each new height h (finish with a sentinel 0), pop every entry greater than h: the arrival of a strictly shorter bar is precisely what stops that rectangle from extending to the right, and the rectangle cannot extend to the left either because the entry below it was strictly smaller (or the stack was empty). Each pop therefore counts one maximal rectangle.

If the top of the stack now equals h the open rectangle just continues over this bar (so equal bars and bars of the same plateau are not counted twice), otherwise push h if it is positive. A zero pops everything and is never pushed. Every bar is pushed and popped at most once, so the time is O(n) and the space O(n).
